newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ACPC may delay coffee export decision - sources.
newsitem.headline: ACPC may delay coffee export decision - sources.

text.p: Major coffee producers set to meet in London next week might delay taking a decision over fresh export quotas in view of significant gains in coffee prices, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"It is most possible that producers will delay a decision on a new export programme," one source said, referring to the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) meeting.
"A decision on the export programme may be postponed for a few months...because of the increase in prices," the source, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
The 14-member ACPC is to review its 12-month export scheme which expires at the end of June at its council meeting on Wednesday.

Members have been asked by the ACPC to consider if they plan to continue with the quota system or devise some other mechanism. The export programme is aimed at capping members' exports at 25.48 million bags in the first half of 1997 through a quota system.
In January, the member countries cut exports by 1.3 million bags but at a subsequent meeting in March, they decided to put back some 500,000 bags back into the market.

Indonesia, the world's third largest producer after Brazil and Colombia, was allocated an export quota of 6.0 million bags under the 1996/97 (July-June) export programme, up from 4.6 million bags in 1995/96.
The London benchmark July robusta coffee contract jumped early in the session on Tuesday to a year-high of $1,835 a tonne but fell back to close at $1,815 for a $40 gain.

Prices of robusta, used mainly in soluble or instant brews, have risen by more than 50 percent since the start of the year on worries about tight supply. Indonesia is the world's top robusta coffee producer.
The sources said Latin American producers were expected to support a delay in any decision on the export programme.
"I think Latin American producers will back delaying any decision on the export programme," one source said.
"We have to give the market enough time to adjust to the new price situation," the source said.

Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, said early last month the country's production this year could be 30 percent short of an original forecast of 480,000 tonnes due to bad weather.
